name: Payor mix
numerator: Pilot employers (or covered lives) choosing each design: employer-paid; employee-paid voluntary; hybrid/shared
denominator: All pilot employers that were offered a documented internet-as-benefit design
unit: percent of employers and percent of lives
gates: Whether anyone other than Charter is willing to fund the line — employer budget vs employee wallet
sequence: Measure at offer / contracting; freeze the mix before OE opens
kill_if: If every (or nearly every) employer refuses employer-paid AND refuses to put a voluntary SKU on the ballot — stop; there is no channel to take up

name: Enrollment take-up by payor
numerator: Enrolled internet accounts attributable to the offer (one account per eligible employee)
denominator: Eligible employees who were offered the benefit and whose address was collected — stratified by M9a payor cell
unit: percent; report separately for employer-paid vs voluntary vs hybrid; never a blended headline
gates: Whether eligible employees actually elect the line once it is on the ballot
sequence: Measure at close of OE plus a 90-day late-enroll window
kill_if: Do not set the numeric floor from analogues. Write the floor before OE. A plausible conservative bound: voluntary take-up in the single-digit to low-teens among eligibles would match lifestyle-voluntary analogues; employer-paid take-up well below KFF medical (76% of eligibles) would be a fail even for a subsidized design. Those bounds are analogues not Charter forecasts.

name: Do not report
gates: A blended enrolled/eligible rate across payor models conceals mix (100% of a tiny employer-paid cell plus 4% of a large voluntary cell can look like a healthy mid-teens rate)
kill_if: Any deliverable that quotes a single M9 take-up number without M9a weights is incomplete
